lem-qa-25-isometry-error-implies-trace-d:
## Statement

Let $V,W:H\to K\otimes E$ be linear isometries between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, meaning $V^*V=W^*W=I_H$, and assume $\delta\ge0$ and $\|V-W\|_{\rm op}\le\delta$. For every nonzero finite-dimensional reference space $R$ and density matrix $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$ (a positive semidefinite matrix of trace one), define $V_R=V\otimes I_R$ and $W_R=W\otimes I_R$ on the ordered product bases. Define the partial trace by
$$(\operatorname{Tr}_E X)_{(k,r),(k',r')}=\sum_e X_{(k,e,r),(k',e,r')},$$
and define $\|X\|_1$ as the sum of singular values and $D(\sigma,\omega)=\tfrac12\|\sigma-\omega\|_1$. The output density matrices
$$\rho_V=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)(V_R\rho V_R^*),\qquad \rho_W=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)(W_R\rho W_R^*)$$
satisfy $D(\rho_V,\rho_W)\le\delta$. Tensor products use the ordered product orthonormal basis and product inner product; the displayed matrix formula fixes the partial-trace convention used here. For column vectors, $a^*$ denotes conjugate transpose and $aa^*$ the rank-one matrix with entries $a_i\overline{a_j}$.
lem-qa-25-parity-path-transfer:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal B_n$ be the complex inner-product space with orthonormal basis $\{|y\rangle:y\in\{0,1\}^n\}$. For $1\le r\le n$, define $X_r|y_1\cdots y_n\rangle=|y_1\cdots(y_r\oplus1)\cdots y_n\rangle$, and put $J=\frac12\sum_{r=1}^nX_r$. For $0\le i\le n$, let $|D_i^n\rangle$ be the normalized uniform sum of basis vectors of Hamming weight $i$; define $\mathcal S_n=\operatorname{span}\{|D_i^n\rangle:0\le i\le n\}$. On a separate path space with orthonormal basis $\{|i\rangle:0\le i\le n\}$, define $H_0$ to have off-diagonal entries $w_i=\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}/n$ between $|i-1\rangle$ and $|i\rangle$ for every 1≤i≤n, and all other matrix entries zero.

Let $n\ge1$, $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $p_0=0,\ p_i=x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_i$. On the basis $\{|i,b\rangle:0\le i\le n,\ b\in\{0,1\}\}$, put
$$H_x=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\sum_{b=0}^1\left(|i-1,b\rangle\langle i,b\oplus x_i|+|i,b\oplus x_i\rangle\langle i-1,b|\right).$$
Write $\operatorname{parity}(x)=p_n=x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_n$. The basis permutation $V_x|i,b\rangle=|i,b\oplus p_i\rangle$ conjugates $H_x$ to two copies of $H_0$. The counting identity proved below gives $H_0=(2/n)J|_{\mathcal S_n}$, under the isometry $|i\rangle\mapsto|D_i^n\rangle$. Consequently $\|H_x\|_{\rm op}\le1$ and
$$e^{-iH_x\pi n/2}|0,0\rangle=(-i)^n|n,\operatorname{parity}(x)\rangle.$$
def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model:
## Definition

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. An **exact Hermitian block encoding** is the data $(U,J,\alpha)$ with $J^*UJ=A$. The matrix $K$ is Hermitian; $U$ itself need not be Hermitian.

The signal-register reflection is $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$. The access record lists, separately, each supplied call to $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, and $R_\Pi$, together with their circuit, query, gate, width, ancilla, precision, and classical-generation costs from [[def-qa-22-block-encoding-access-model]] and [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A state description or block matrix alone supplies none of these calls. A controlled reflection is also separate. Any PREPARE, SELECT, sparse-location, value, or coefficient operation used by a construction is a separately supplied, reversible interface with its inverse and cost recorded.

Here is the standard-form **qubiterate** for this access instance. Add a flag qubit and define $\widetilde U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes U+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U^*$, $J'v=|+\rangle\otimes Jv$, $S=X\otimes I$, $F=S\widetilde U$, and $W_{\mathrm q}=(2J'J'^*-I)F$. Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].
def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynom:
## Definition

For a finite Hermitian $H$ with exact block-encoding normalization $\alpha>0$, $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$, and real time $t$, put $\tau=\alpha t$. On $x\in[-1,1]$ the scalar target is $f_\tau(x)=\exp(-i\tau x)$; if $H\psi_\lambda=\lambda\psi_\lambda$, then $f_\tau(\lambda/\alpha)=\exp(-it\lambda)$, the eigenvalue of the finite matrix evolution [[def-qa-19-finite-matrix-dynamics]].

For $k\ge0$, define the Chebyshev polynomials by $T_0(x)=1$, $T_1(x)=x$, $T_{k+1}(x)=2xT_k(x)-T_{k-1}(x)$. Define the Bessel coefficients used here by the series
$$J_k(\tau)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^j(\tau/2)^{2j+k}}{j!(j+k)!}.$$
For fixed $k,\tau$, the ratio of consecutive absolute summands is $\tau^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]\to0$, so this series converges absolutely and defines $J_k(\tau)$ before any estimate is used. The exponential uses the series convention of [[def-complex-exponential]], whose absolute convergence is supplied by [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]. This definition specifies the target and coefficient series; it does not assert a Jacobi–Anger expansion or a truncation bound. A real QSP or QSVT theorem alone does not implement this full complex, non-parity target; the finite even/odd combination, complementary-polynomial certificates, normalization, and controlled relative phase are separate operations in the binding simulator.
lem-qa-25-hermitian-block-encoding-signa:
## Statement

Let $(U,J,\alpha)$ be an exact Hermitian block encoding from [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], and choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $K\psi_j=\lambda_j\psi_j$. Put $x_j=\lambda_j/\alpha$ and $s_j=\sqrt{1-x_j^2}$. For $|x_j|<1$, define
$$\eta_j=(I-\Pi)UJ\psi_j/s_j,\qquad \widetilde\eta_j=(I-\Pi)U^*J\psi_j/s_j.$$
The $\eta_j$ are orthonormal in $\ker\Pi$, as are the $\widetilde\eta_j$. In the paired input basis $(J\psi_j,\widetilde\eta_j)$ and output basis $(J\psi_j,\eta_j)$, $U$ has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}x_j&s_j\\s_j&-x_j\end{pmatrix}.$$
The unitary $U^*$ maps in the reverse direction by the same matrix. If $|x_j|=1$, the complement is absent and $UJ\psi_j=x_jJ\psi_j=U^*J\psi_j$; no division by zero is used. The value $x_j=0$ is an ordinary two-dimensional signal plane.
thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence:
## Statement

Let $(U,J,\alpha)$ be an exact Hermitian block encoding of $K$, with $K=K^*$ and $\|K\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$. The qubiterate $W_{\rm q}$ of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]] has, on each eigenvalue $x=\lambda/\alpha$, a two-dimensional invariant signal space on which it is a rotation with eigenvalues $e^{\pm i\arccos x}$; at $x=\pm1$ the space collapses to the corresponding eigenline.

For a phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$, alternating $U,U^*$ calls and projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ acts on each paired signal space as the scalar Hermitian-reflection QSP sequence $U_\Phi(x)$ of [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. If $P_\Phi$ is its upper-left polynomial, the clean compressed block is $P_\Phi(K/\alpha)$ on all eigenspaces simultaneously, with the endpoint and null directions handled by the same polynomial evaluation. Admissible phases are supplied by [[thm-qa-23-qsp-phase-factorization]]; translating to the SU(2) convention carries the scalar $i^d$, which remains a relative phase under control.
thm-qa-25-bounded-error-parity-query-low:
## Statement

Any quantum query algorithm that, on every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, outputs $\operatorname{parity}(x)$ with error at most $1/3$ using the coherent XOR oracle for $x$ makes at least $n/2$ oracle queries.
alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulati:
## Definition

**Inputs.** A finite Hermitian $H$, $\alpha>0$, an exact $(\alpha,a,0)$ block encoding $U$ with $J^*UJ=H/\alpha$, a rational time $t$, rational $0<\epsilon\le1$, and separately declared access and cost for $U,U^*,$ controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, both projector-phase circuits, coefficient preparation, SELECT, OAA reflections, phase synthesis, data access, and classical arithmetic. The input description also supplies terminating certified comparisons and rational-interval evaluations for the scalar arithmetic below. A bounded block-error input is a separate variant with a certified block-error budget; it is not silently treated as exact.

**Output.** Return the finite circuit list and error certificate for a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$. Its success claim is on the clean-input isometry $J_{\rm clean}|\psi\rangle=|0_{\rm work}\rangle|\psi\rangle$; auxiliary output registers are approximate and are not measured to clean an unknown system input. On a failed polynomial or phase certificate, return the phase routine's declared failure status and do not report a simulator.

**Generation and execution.** Set $\tau=\alpha t$ and $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$. For $t=0$, return the identity circuit and zero query count. Otherwise:

1. Starting at $d=\max(1,\lceil|\tau|\rceil)$, increase $d$ until $u=|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$ and
   $$\frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!(1-u)}\le\rho/8.$$
   Evaluate each strict comparison by the certified interval routine named in OP0 of the binding operational appendix; an undecided equality is not rounded toward success.
2. For each $k=0,\ldots,d$, compute $J_k(\tau)$ from the series in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]]. Stop its alternating-series evaluation only after its ratio $\tau^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]$ is below $1$ and its geometric remainder is at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$. Store a rational coefficient and its error interval. Form $T_0=1,T_1=x,T_{k+1}=2xT_k-T_{k-1}$. Set
   $$E=J_0+2\sum_{1\le 2r\le d}(-1)^rJ_{2r}T_{2r},\qquad O=2\sum_{1\le 2r+1\le d}(-1)^rJ_{2r+1}T_{2r+1}.$$
   Thus $Q:=E-iO$ is the rounded Jacobi–Anger truncation and its certified scalar error is $\|Q-f_\tau\|_{[-1,1]}\le\rho$; the sign $(-i)^k$ is literal.
3. Require a certified combined polynomial error at most $\rho$. Then $|E(x)|,|O(x)|\le1+\rho$ on $[-1,1]$. Put $B=1+2\rho$, $p_E=E/B$, and $p_O=O/B$. Call [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]] separately on these two real targets with their actual degree and parity, retaining its complementary-polynomial certificate, phase list, precision, and every explicit failure branch. Execute each real QSVT extraction using [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]] and the exact signal access of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]]. If an extraction fails certification, return that failure.
4. Pad both extraction workspaces to the same ordered register space. Prepare a clean coefficient qubit in $|+\rangle$. SELECT applies the $p_E(H/\alpha)$ block in branch $0$ and $-i$ times the $p_O(H/\alpha)$ block in branch $1$. Unprepare the coefficient qubit. The resulting clean block before amplification is $M/2$, where $M=p_E(H/\alpha)-i p_O(H/\alpha)=Q(H/\alpha)/B$. Since $B=1+2\rho$, the scalar error bound gives
$$\|M-e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\frac{\rho}{B}+\frac{B-1}{B}=\frac{3\rho}{1+2\rho}<3\rho;$$
here $f_\tau(H/\alpha)=e^{-itH}$ by finite spectral calculus and $|f_\tau(x)|=1$. The factor $-i$ is a relative phase under any outer control and is not discarded.
5. Apply the explicit phase-corrected oblivious-amplitude-amplification unitary $C=-WRW^*RW$, where $R=I-2\Pi_{\rm zero}$ and $W$ is the complete even/odd block-combination circuit. Retain its work registers. Allocate total phase, gate, and block implementation error at most $\epsilon/4$ after amplification. A controlled simulator controls every whole block and the known correction, using the separately supplied controlled access.

The arithmetic, coefficient series, two phase-generation calls, controlled QSVT sequences, coefficient register, SELECT, and OAA list are finite outputs; their gate, query, precision, workspace, description-bit, and classical computation costs are separate coordinates. The phase-generation call is the finite procedure of [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]], not a free source routine. A sparse input uses its actually supplied block-encoding circuit and its exact row-location, value, precision, and state-preparation costs; standard XOR sparse access alone does not imply an in-place reversible location permutation.
lem-qa-25-sorted-xor-sparse-access-isome:
## Statement

Let $H$ have the exact sorted $d$-sparse Hermitian XOR-location/value interface of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], with $N,d\ge1$. An optional support-list variant is also admissible: each row lists at most $d$ distinct columns in strictly increasing order, contains every nonzero column exactly once, and may additionally list zero-valued columns. Its row and column support lists agree under transposition; in the Hermitian case the row list at $j$ supplies the column list at $j$. The total XOR value oracle gives the exact decoded matrix, including any listed zeros. Missing slots use the same distinguished sentinel. No zero test on the matrix values is needed to form a supplied support union. An approximation to a different target matrix requires a separate operator-error bound. Put $M=2^{\lceil\log_2(N+d)\rceil}$ and $\widetilde H=H\oplus0$ on the $M$-label register. Given a positive certified bound $h\ge\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$, an exact costed preparation $d^{-1/2}\sum_{l<d}|l\rangle$, and costed exact value-decoding and flag-rotation arithmetic, one can construct a unitary whose clean block is $\widetilde H/(dh)$. It and its actual adjoint and coherent controlled versions use $O(\log(d+1))$ QA20 location calls and $O(1)$ value calls each. Index bits, reversible workspace, search arithmetic, comparisons, uniform preparation, flags and gate precision remain separately charged. In particular $h=1$ is admissible when $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le1$, without computing the global maximum entry. The stronger separately supplied in-place-location interface keeps its original constant location-call count.
lem-qa-25-clean-subspace-unitary-hybrid:
## Statement

Let $J:H\to K$ be an isometry of nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, $V$ a unitary on $H$, and $U$ a unitary on $K$. If $\|UJ-JV\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$, then $\|U^*J-JV^*\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$. The same inequalities hold after adjoining an arbitrary finite reference space or coherently controlling $U$ and $V$ against identity.

More generally, let $U_1,\ldots,U_s$ be actual unitaries on $K$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_s$ ideal unitaries on $H$, with $\|U_jJ-JV_j\|_{\rm op}\le\eta_j$. Then
$$\|U_s\cdots U_1J-JV_s\cdots V_1\|_{\rm op}\le\sum_{j=1}^s\eta_j.$$
The empty products give zero error. Each bound concerns the clean input subspace $\operatorname{ran}J$; none assumes that an actual intermediate state belongs to that subspace or claims a full-space approximation on arbitrary dirty-work inputs.
alg-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encod:
## Definition

**Input.** A finite $d_H$-row-sparse Hermitian matrix $H$, with $d_H\ge1$, and $h_{\max}=\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|\ge0$. Supply exact row and column enumerations, each listing every nonzero entry exactly once and padded to $d_H$ distinct labels with sentinels that never create a good-flag overlap; supply reversible in-place permutations $O_r,O_c$ and their inverses, each with its actual query and gate costs. Supply an exact unitary $D_{d_H}$ preparing $d_H^{-1/2}\sum_{k=1}^{d_H}|k\rangle$, its inverse, and their costs. A classical table is not a free state-preparation circuit. If $h_{\max}=0$, use one flag qubit and return $X_{\rm flag}\otimes I$ with normalization $1$; its all-zero flag compression is $0=H$. Otherwise set $\alpha=d_Hh_{\max}$.

**Instructions when $h_{\max}>0$.** Put $\widehat H=H/h_{\max}$, so every queried entry $h_{ij}=\widehat H_{ij}$ obeys $|h_{ij}|\le1$. On the paired row/column index registers define
$$V_L=O_r(I\otimes D_{d_H})\,\mathrm{SWAP},\qquad V_R=O_c(D_{d_H}\otimes I).$$
Let $U_L=I_{\rm flag}\otimes V_L$. Define $U_R$ by first applying $V_R$, then querying $h_{ij}$, applying to the flag
$$\begin{pmatrix} h_{ij}&-\sqrt{1-|h_{ij}|^2}\\ \sqrt{1-|h_{ij}|^2}&\overline{h_{ij}} \end{pmatrix},$$
and unquerying the value and arithmetic workspace. The square root is the nonnegative real root. Invalid sentinel pairs use $h_{ij}=0$. Return $U_L^*U_R$ with the all-zero auxiliary block designated as the encoded block. Every index, flag, value, state-preparation, inverse, controlled, arithmetic, and finite-precision operation is supplied or charged separately.

The supplied-permutation mode requires the in-place location permutations as explicit input. The total XOR row-location oracle of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]] does not itself supply an $O(1)$-query in-place permutation or its inverse. Any scan or inverse-location construction must be specified and charged before claiming such a sparse-oracle cost.

The block identity and its exact query accounting are proved in [[thm-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding-correctness]].

**Sorted-XOR specialization.** As an alternative input mode, supply the exact sorted XOR location/value interface of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], or the sorted distinct support-superset variant allowing listed zero entries in [[lem-qa-25-sorted-xor-sparse-access-isometries]], a certified positive bound $h\ge\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$, and the same separately charged uniform preparation and value/flag arithmetic. Execute the explicit compute-location, binary-search inverse, slot-erasure and row/column-overlap construction of [[lem-qa-25-sorted-xor-sparse-access-isometries]]. It pads the system to $M=2^{\lceil\log_2(N+d_H)\rceil}$ and returns a clean block encoding of $(H\oplus0)/(d_Hh)$, with normalization $\alpha=d_Hh$. The location workspace is exactly clean on every prepared slot state. Each encoding, actual adjoint or coherent controlled encoding costs $O(\log(d_H+1))$ original location calls and $O(1)$ value calls; its sorting assumption is part of this mode's input. If $\|H\|\le1$, choose $h=1$ without computing a maximum. Keep the one-sided value amplitude on $U_R$ exactly as above. The original supplied-permutation mode and its sharper call count remain available.
thm-qa-25-sparse-no-fast-forwarding-lowe:
## Statement

For $n\ge1$, let $H_x$ be the $2(n+1)$-dimensional, at-most-two-sparse Hermitian path matrix of [[lem-qa-25-parity-path-transfer]] for $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, with weights $w_i=\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}/n$. Put $\eta=1/(6\pi n)$, choose $b=\lceil\log_2(3\pi n)\rceil$, and round each nonzero weight to the nearest dyadic $q_i=2^{-b}\operatorname{round}(2^bw_i)$, with ties rounded upward. Let $\widetilde H_x$ be the same path matrix with weights $q_i$, and encode its entries exactly in the row-location/value XOR-oracle model of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], using $O(\log(n+1))$ value bits for the finite set $\{0,q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$. Then $\|H_x-\widetilde H_x\|_{\rm op}\le2\eta$ and the sparse normalization $\alpha_{\rm sp}=2\max_i q_i$ lies between positive absolute constants.

Suppose a uniform sparse-oracle query algorithm uses $q$ total row-location and value-oracle calls and returns a clean-input isometry $V_xJ_{\rm clean}$ satisfying
$$\|V_xJ_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-it\widetilde H_x}\|_{\rm op}\le\tfrac13, \qquad t=\pi n/2,$$
where $J_{\rm out}$ appends its work registers in zero. Then $q\ge n/4$. Thus this sparse row/value model requires $\Omega(n)=\Omega(t)=\Omega(\alpha_{\rm sp}t)$ queries for this family. The result does not assert a lower bound for arbitrary block-encoding access.
alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator:
## Definition

**Input.** An exact Hermitian block encoding of $H/\alpha$, $\alpha>0$, a rational time $t$, $0<\epsilon<1$, and a terminating certified comparison of $\tau=\alpha|t|$ with $\epsilon$, charged under the access model.

**Instructions.**

1. If $\tau\le\epsilon$, return the identity circuit on the system, with every work register left at zero. The query, gate, and bit costs of this branch are zero.
2. If $\tau>\epsilon$, invoke [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] with $t,\epsilon$, and return its circuit and error certificate. Propagate any INVALID, CERTIFICATE_ERROR, or IMPLEMENTATION_ERROR result without labeling it a successful simulation.

The comparison cost is recorded separately. The second branch is exactly the OP4 procedure; this wrapper does not modify OP4 or infer inverse, controlled, state-preparation, or phase-synthesis access.
thm-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encod:
## Statement

For a nonzero $d_H$-row-sparse Hermitian $H$, the designated all-zero auxiliary compression of $U_L^*U_R$ from [[alg-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding]] is $H/(d_Hh_{\max})$. In the zero case the returned $X_{\rm flag}\otimes I$ has zero all-zero-flag compression and normalization $1$. One nonzero-case block-encoding call uses one supplied inverse row-location permutation, one supplied column-location permutation, two entry-value queries (compute and uncompute), and the declared $D_{d_H}$, inverse, flag-rotation, and arithmetic implementations. In the optional sorted-XOR mode the encoded matrix is $H\oplus0$ with normalization $d_Hh$ for the supplied positive entry bound $h$, and each encoding, actual adjoint or coherent controlled call costs $O(\log(d_H+1))$ original location calls and $O(1)$ value calls. No constant-cost conversion from XOR locations to in-place permutations is asserted.
lem-qa-25-jacobi-anger-truncation:
## Statement

With $J_k,T_k$ defined in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]], for every real $\tau$ and integer $d\ge0$,
$$\sup_{|x|\le1}\left|\exp(-i\tau x)-\left(J_0(\tau)+2\sum_{k=1}^{d}(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)T_k(x)\right)\right| \le 2\sum_{k>d}|J_k(\tau)| \le \frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!\left(1-|\tau|/(2(d+2))\right)}$$
whenever $|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$. In the OP4 simulator, $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$ and the factorial-tail stopping test therefore certifies truncation error at most $\rho/8$; rounding each coefficient to error at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$ keeps the combined polynomial error below $\rho$. For the nontrivial simulation regime $|\tau|>\epsilon$, an integer $d$ passing OP4's test exists with
$$d=O\left(|\tau|+\frac{\ln(1/\epsilon)}{\ln(e+\ln(1/\epsilon)/|\tau|)}\right).$$
For $|\tau|\le\epsilon$, the constant polynomial $1$ approximates the target within $\epsilon$; the wrapper algorithm uses the exact identity circuit in that branch.
thm-qa-25-qubitized-simulation-correctne:
## Statement

For the exact access model of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], rational $t$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$, a successful execution of [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] returns a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$ satisfying
$$\|V_{\rm impl}J_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$$
on the clean-input isometry $J_{\rm clean}$, where $J_{\rm out}$ appends every work register in zero. Output work registers are approximate; no full-space error on arbitrary dirty work inputs or exact cleanup is asserted. For $t=0$, the declared identity branch is exact. For every reference system, tracing out work gives the corresponding system-output trace-distance bound at most $\epsilon$.
thm-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator-cor:
## Statement

For every promised input of [[alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator]], a successful output satisfies the clean-input isometry error bound $\|V_{\rm impl}J_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$. It also satisfies the corresponding reference-system trace-distance bound after tracing the work registers.
thm-qa-25-qubitized-simulation-resource-:
## Statement

Let $\tau=\alpha|t|$, $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)$, and $S=\tau+L/\ln(e+L/\tau)$, with $0<\epsilon<1$. The small-time-aware simulator of [[alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator]] uses zero signal queries when $\tau\le\epsilon$. When $\tau>\epsilon$, the OP4 degree satisfies $d=O(S)$. The complete OAA circuit uses at most $3(d_E+d_O)\le6d$ ordinary $U/U^*$ signal calls, where $d_E,d_O\le d$ are the even and odd QSP degrees. It uses $3(d_E+d_O+2)$ projector-phase slots and therefore $6(d_E+d_O+2)$ controlled-reflection calls, by [[thm-qa-24-qsvt-query-count]]. Coherent selection of each real sequence against identity uses exactly one controlled signal call when that sequence degree is odd and none when it is even; because the selection occurs in each of the three OAA blocks $W,W^*,W$, the total is $3(\mathbf1_{d_E\text{ odd}}+\mathbf1_{d_O\text{ odd}})\le6$ controlled signal calls. The $\Phi/-\Phi$ branch itself controls phases, not signal calls. Any external control of the complete simulator controls and charges the whole block.

Gate, depth, width, ancilla, classical bit, precision, PREPARE/SELECT, phase-list-generation, and sparse-location/value costs remain separate coordinates. For a $d_H$-row-sparse input, [[thm-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding-correctness]] gives normalization $\alpha=d_Hh_{\max}$; multiply the signal-query count by the actual supplied sparse-encoding cost, including any location-permutation completion. The optional sorted-XOR mode instead has normalization $d_Hh$ for a supplied positive entry bound $h$ and multiplies the signal count by $O(\log(d_H+1))$ location calls and $O(1)$ value calls per signal, including inverses and coherent controls. No cost-free conversion from XOR row-location access is claimed. If $\tau$ is bounded above and below by positive constants as $\epsilon\to0$, the query bound specializes to $O(\tau+L/\ln L)=O(\tau+\ln(1/\epsilon)/\ln\ln(1/\epsilon))$. This is an upper bound; no matching lower bound for arbitrary block-encoding access or for the additive precision term is asserted.
